teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner replaces /θ/ (think) with /s/ or /f/.
💡 Solution: Stick tongue tip out between front teeth and blow unvoiced air.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Basic Consonant Digraphs (SH, CH, TH, PH, WH, NG, CK)
1. Definition: A consonant digraph is two consonant letters that join together to make one single sound.
2. Rule: SH = /ʃ/ (ship), CH = /tʃ/ (chat), TH = /θ/ (think) or /ð/ (the), PH = /f/ (phone), WH = /w/ (what), NG = /ŋ/ (sing), CK = /k/ (back).
3. Why? Historical sound shifts created single phonemes represented by letter pairs.
4. How to recognize? Spot letter pairs sh, ch, th, ph, wh, ng, ck.
5. Common examples: ship, fish, child, much, think, the, phone, what, sing, back, kick
6. Counter-examples: Separate consonants across syllable boundary (mishap = mis-hap).
7. Exceptions: CH = /k/ in Greek words (school) and /ʃ/ in French words (chef).
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing T and H separately in 'think' instead of placing tongue between teeth.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Two letters, ONE brand new sound!
10. Key vocabulary: digraph, consonant team, voiced, voiceless, tongue placement
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟢 A1
13. Associated Visual: 🤝 Two consonant letters shaking hands to form one sound.
14. Key Takeaway: Digraphs make 1 sound! Put tongue between teeth for TH.

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: How many sounds do the two letters S and H make in 'ship'? (One sound: /ʃ/)
CCQ 2: Where is your tongue when you say TH in 'think'? (Between your teeth)
CCQ 3: When do we use CK instead of K? (After a short vowel at the end of a word)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Read these digraph words and classify the sound:
🎯 Item: ship ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /ʃ/ (SH)
🎯 Item: think vs the ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Voiceless /θ/ vs Voiced /ð/
🎯 Item: back ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /k/ (CK after short vowel)
